question.text: A microscope was initially placed in air (refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>). It is then immersed in oil (refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>). For a light whose wavelength in air is $\lambda$, calculate the change of microscope's resolving power due to oil and choose the correct option

options.text: Resolving power will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> in the oil than it was in the air
Resolving power will be twice in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be four times in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> in the oil than it was in the air.

solution.text:
Resolving power of microscope in air is (R.P)air =2μairsinθ1.22λ=2sinθ1.22λ

(R.P)oil =2μoilsinθ1.22λoil =2sinθ21.22λ

R.Poil=R.Pair×2

Thus, resolving power in oil is twice the resolving power in air.
